dedupe_keys.name: emergency telecommunications cluster operations during the 2014 ebola emergency in guinea liberia and sierra leone service sites

description: During the 2014 Ebola emergency in West Africa, the Emergency Telecommunications Cluster, led by the World Food Programme, set up data connectivity and radio services for responders. The U.S. Department of State's Humanitarian Information Unit mapped the services provided by the cluster in each affected country and published three small shapefiles on the Humanitarian Data Exchange, one each for Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone, dated 2 December 2014. Each layer marks the sites where the cluster provided services, such as internet connectivity and security telecommunications at humanitarian hubs, Ebola treatment units and logistics bases, with service type attributes; forward and main logistics bases were served by the UN Mission for Ebola Emergency Response (UNMEER) and the UN Mission in Liberia with cluster support. Coverage: Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone. Format and access: zipped shapefiles of about 2 KB each, free under CC0 (public domain). Caveats: a one-day snapshot of a fast-changing operation; very few points per country; attribute meanings are not documented beyond the title. Simulation uses: a reference case for deploying emergency connectivity to response sites during an epidemic, for humanitarian communication planning models. Related records: the Guinea localities covered by telecom networks give the commercial coverage baseline; the ITU national emergency telecommunication plans record describes planning guidance; the Tonga cable cut case study describes a later cluster activation.
